searchText: Will l2 solutions really be obselete with eth2.0? Lets say sharding,transitioning to PoS, and rollups are achieved, wouldnt l2 solutions provide even higher tps and lower gas fees? L2 = rollups They're already live Sharding will take atleast 2 years, it's not guaranteed it's even happening yet. What about eth native rollups? Doesn't look like that's happening anytime soon Yea thats what i thought. Thanks. It's the other way round - rollups obsoleted "Eth 2.0" execution sharding before it even existed for precisely the reason you mention. "Eth 2.0" no longer exists, and Ethereum is going with a rollup-centric roadmap. Sharding on the current roadmap is purely for data availability (what was previously Phase 1) - these data shards will be used to accelerate rollups, you won't be able to do any transactions on them. My speculation is that we'll never see the old fraud-proven execution sharding model (what was previously Phase 2), and instead head straight to zkEVM on L1 in a few years' time. Wait so the preliminary sharding docs in the eth2.0-specs repo is completely outdated now? wut? if you're replying to "what about eth native rollups" i'm confused The repo called consensus-specs now, and the specs there was always data sharding (previously Phase 1) i broadly agree that execution is not being pursued, with the caveat of "for now." roadmaps are flexible, can and do change, as we saw with the merge prioritization the eth2 deprecated nomenclature wasn't so much linked to rollups, as it was to the desire to unify everthing under the same common scheme, which the merge gives us Fair enough, things can change, and that's why I called it "my speculation" so is sharded execution still probably happening?
